summary: Learn QGIS watershed preparation, remote-sensing inputs, and HEC-HMS runoff modeling. Review the 10-day course outline and enrol.
lede: Hydrological modeling combines spatial data and rainfall-runoff methods to estimate watershed response and assess runoff scenarios. For hydrology, GIS, and water-resources professionals, this foundation-level course develops practical workflows to prepare terrain and land-cover inputs, delineate watersheds in QGIS, and configure HEC-HMS simulations. You will also organize rainfall data and review calibration results, model performance, and uncertainty when observed streamflow is available.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who prepare or review watershed data, rainfall-runoff models, and related water-resources evidence. It suits foundation-level learners who need a structured introduction to QGIS and HEC-HMS workflows. This course is designed for: Hydrologists preparing rainfall-runoff estimates for watershed planning. GIS analysts creating DEM-derived drainage and catchment layers. Water-resources engineers assessing runoff scenarios for infrastructure planning. Hydrology technicians organizing rainfall and streamflow observations for modeling. Remote-sensing analysts classifying land cover for hydrologic model inputs. Flood-risk analysts comparing catchment runoff outputs with observed evidence. Watershed project officers assembling spatial datasets for basin assessments. Environmental consultants preparing hydrology inputs for project impact studies. Water utility planning officers reviewing catchment inflow assumptions. Agricultural drainage specialists estimating runoff from changing land cover.
prerequisites: Basic numeracy and familiarity with maps are useful. Prior hydrological modeling, GIS, and programming experience are not required. Coding is not required to complete the course.
